newsitem.title: USA: Key adversaries to face off on muni pay-to-play.
newsitem.headline: Key adversaries to face off on muni pay-to-play.

text.p: Two key opponents in the debate over whether tough new voluntary curbs are needed to stem pay-to-play by bond attorneys are scheduled to face off at a National Association of Bond Lawyers (NABL) luncheon on May 8, a NABL official said.

Michael Cardozo, president of the Association of the Bar of the City of New York, will debate Lawrence Fox, chairman of the American Bar Association's standing committee on ethics and professional responsibility, on the volatile issue at the 1215 EDT luncheon on day one of NABL's two-day Washington Seminar set for May 8-9, the official said.
The upcoming session appears to be the "first time they are going to go head to head" on the issue, added Amy Dunbar, NABL's director of governmental affairs, regarding Cardozo and Fox.

Cordozo's group wants ABA to endorse a rule approved by the City bar last year that would prohibit muni lawyers who solicit or make contributions to municipal clients, including some PAC contributions, from engaging in bond business for two years with those governments.
The rule is partly modeled after a standard adopted by the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board in 1994 for muni bond dealers, although the City bar's rule is more restrictive.

But Fox's panel last week sent a letter to the chairs of all ABA standing committees and sections urging the officials to reject the City bar's initiative when ABA delegates vote on it at ABA's annual meeting in August.

"We want to air the issues for our members," said Dunbar, whose group has come under criticism from SEC officials for not developing a tougher stand on the pay-to-play issue. The group has endorsed a policy that law firms disclose contributions to issuer officials.
